content.value_statement: Complex systems often mix writes and reads, limiting scalability and clarity. This skill guides separate models, projections, synchronization, and consistency decisions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies command, query, handler, event, and projection boundaries.
Provides Python templates for command buses and query buses.
Demonstrates parameterized read model queries and pagination.
Shows FastAPI endpoints separated by command and query responsibilities.
Explains projection rebuilding, checkpoints, and read-your-writes handling.
limitations: Does not provide a complete deployable application or infrastructure configuration.
Uses Python and FastAPI examples that require adaptation for other stacks.
Does not select databases, brokers, or event stores for a specific environment.
Cannot replace load testing, recovery testing, or domain expert review.

use_cases.title: Separate a Growing Service
use_cases.description: Map an existing service into commands, queries, handlers, and independently optimized data models.

use_cases.title: Plan Scalable Read Models
use_cases.description: Design projections, checkpoints, pagination, and synchronization for workloads with heavy reporting demand.

use_cases.title: Review Consistency Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Define acceptable projection lag, read-your-writes behavior, rebuild procedures, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Identify CQRS Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this application description: [description]. Identify commands, queries, handlers, and read models. Explain whether CQRS is justified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when first evaluating CQRS for a service.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CQRS Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CQRS flow for [feature]. Include command validation, emitted events, query models, projection updates, and consistency expectations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when planning one bounded feature.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the Implementation Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the CQRS patterns to [language and framework]. Preserve parameterized queries, handler boundaries, projection checkpoints, and explicit failure behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when translating the provided Python examples.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production CQRS Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CQRS design: [design]. Assess idempotency, ordering, retries, projection rebuilds, schema evolution, observability, consistency targets, and recovery risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before production rollout or a major architecture change.

output_examples.input: Design CQRS boundaries for an order service with heavy customer reporting.
output: Commands: create order, add item, and cancel order.
Queries: retrieve an order, list customer orders, and search orders.
Read model: denormalized order views optimized for reporting.
Consistency: asynchronous projections with defined lag and checkpoint monitoring.

output_examples.input: Review a projection that can restart after processing failures.
output_examples.output: Track durable checkpoints, make event application idempotent, retry transient failures, isolate invalid events, and test full projection rebuilds.

output_examples.input: Decide whether a simple inventory tool needs CQRS.
output_examples.output: Keep a conventional CRUD design when workloads are modest, models are similar, and immediate consistency is required throughout.

best_practices: Define consistency targets and acceptable projection lag before implementation.
Keep command validation, event persistence, and query retrieval responsibilities explicit.
Test projection idempotency, checkpoint recovery, and complete rebuild procedures.
anti_patterns: Do not introduce separate models when simple CRUD meets the requirements.
Do not share persistence schemas tightly between command and query paths.
Do not ignore ordering, retries, duplicate events, or stale read behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill help implement?
faq.answer: It guides command and query separation, handler design, read model projections, synchronization, and consistency handling.

faq.question: Does this skill require event sourcing?
faq.answer: No. CQRS can use conventional persistence, although the playbook includes event-driven patterns.

faq.question: Which technology stack does it demonstrate?
faq.answer: The detailed examples use Python, asynchronous database access, and FastAPI.

faq.question: When should CQRS be avoided?
faq.answer: Avoid it when CRUD is sufficient, separate models are impractical, or immediate consistency is required everywhere.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. Teams must choose infrastructure, complete integrations, and validate performance and recovery in their environment.

faq.question: How does it address eventual consistency?
faq.answer: It covers projection checkpoints, synchronization loops, rebuilds, expected versions, timeouts, and stale-data warnings.
